title: What If You Drank Way Too Much Water?

scenes.text: What if you drank way too much water, too fast? The danger isn't your stomach. It's your brain.
Your kidneys can only clear about one litre an hour. Drink faster, and the extra stays in your blood.
That water dilutes the sodium in your blood. When it drops too low, doctors call it hyponatremia.
Your cells swell with water. Most can stretch, but your brain is locked in a skull with almost no room.
Headache, nausea and confusion come first. In one Boston Marathon study, 13 percent of runners tested had low sodium.
Water keeps you alive. Too much, too fast, does the opposite.

description:
What if you drank way too much water, too fast? Healthy kidneys clear roughly 0.8 to 1 litre an hour; drinking faster dilutes blood sodium (hyponatremia, below 135 mmol/L), and cells, including brain cells, swell.
Symptoms run from headache, nausea and confusion to seizures and coma in severe cases. A 2005 NEJM study found 13 percent of 488 runners in the 2002 Boston Marathon had hyponatremia.
